stem:
Amaya looks at the diagram. Point $O$ lies on a straight line, and a right angle is to be built at $O$.

Which plan correctly constructs the $90^\circ$ angle at $O$?

options.text: Mark points $X$ and $Y$ on the line at equal distances from $O$ so that $O$ is the midpoint of $XY$, then construct the perpendicular bisector of $XY$.
Keep $O$ on the line and draw any upright ray from $O$.
First draw a line that looks upright through $O$, then mark equal distances from $O$.
Treat $O$ as a point off the line and drop a perpendicular from outside.

teacher.key_rationale: A 90° at O on a line is made by taking O as midpoint of a segment on the line, then erecting the perpendicular bisector. Skipping the midpoint step, reversing the order, or treating O as off the line miss that construction.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle as line with midpoint O of XY and perpendicular at O marked 90°.
